Section C: Crime, deviance and social control

text: Experiences of schooling can be very diverse and this can affect educational achievement. For
example the type of school attended and the student’s family background can be very important.
Some sociologists believe that every student has the chance to be successful in education, others
think this is impossible due to educational inequality.

Section D: Media

text: Many people believe that stricter controls are needed in order to reduce the problem of crime in
society. Different explanations have been offered for why crime occurs, ranging from inadequate
socialisation to relative deprivation. Some sociologists also think that the formal agencies of social
control are unfair and do not treat everybody in the same way.

text: In many countries there is public service broadcasting. However, some media is controlled by
private companies who make large profits. Audiences consume the media in different ways and
patterns of use are quite diverse. Whether the content of the media influences the audience’s
behaviour and attitudes remains a matter of debate.
